title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

findings.explanation: The change only refactors Django ORM queryset filtering logic. No raw SQL queries or string interpolation of user input into SQL is involved.

The refactoring changes the logic when both `admin=True` and `member=True` are passed. The original code built a union filter `Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) | Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS)` and applied it in a single `.filter()` call alongside `teams__members=user`, ensuring the team membership and access-level constraints were checked together in one join. The new code first filters by `teams__members=user` and then — when both flags are True — skips the access-level filter entirely (the `else: pass` branch). This means any team membership satisfies the query regardless of access level, which is the same semantically as the original union when both flags are True, so it is likely intentional. However, the ORM join semantics differ slightly: the original single `.filter()` ensured both `teams__members=user` AND the access predicate referred to the *same* team row, whereas chained `.filter()` calls in Django can match across different related rows. In the new code the `else` branch omits the access filter entirely, which broadens the set of projects returned — a user who is a member of a team with no recognized access level could gain access to projects they shouldn't. This is a possible authorization flaw rather than a confirmed one, because it depends on whether teams can have access values outside ADMIN_ACCESS/READ_ONLY_ACCESS in practice.
findings.suggested_fix: When both `admin` and `member` are True, explicitly filter with the union of both access levels to avoid accidentally including teams with unexpected access values: `projects_from_teams = projects_from_teams.filter(Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) | Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS))`. Also consider using a single `.filter()` call with a combined Q expression (as in the original) to preserve correct Django ORM join semantics.
